subject: Dedicated pool starvation — escalation & mitigation planning
messages:
From: Maria Alvarez <maria@cobaltpay.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-lead@cobaltpay.com
Date: 2026-09-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in latency / errors — CobaltPay Reserved pool impact

Hi Tessa,

We're seeing a sustained increase in 5xx errors and tail latency across our production endpoints that started Friday night (around 03:00 UTC). Throughput has dropped even though our Dedicated reservation shows as active in the console. Our customers are seeing failed transactions and we're outside our SLA window on several routes.

What we observed:
- 5xx rate jumped from ~0.2% to 4% between 03:00–06:30 UTC on 2026-09-19.
- Median latency up ~3x; p95 latency doubled.
- Queueing and token-throttle events in the app logs aligned to the same window.

We've attached an error snapshot and a short set of logs. Please escalate — this is impacting merchant payouts and ops are in the loop. We need a mitigation plan and ETA for a durable fix.

Thanks,
Maria Alvarez
Head of Platform Reliability
CobaltPay

Attachment: error_snapshot.json (snippet)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in latency / errors — CobaltPay Reserved pool impact

Team — forwarding CobaltPay's report. Internal participants only: Marissa (AM), Aditya (sales), David (infra).

Customer reporting Dedicated reservation not protecting throughput; 5xx and latency spike. Can infra confirm whether this is noisy-neighbor, reservation drift, or SDK/route config change (e.g. unexpected batching) on our side?

Immediate asks:
- Quick triage summary (within 30m) with root-cause hypothesis.
- Confirm whether we can temporarily route CobaltPay traffic to a hosted-compatible variant or apply a reserved burst allotment.
- If capacity reallocation is required, we need an exact time window and an exec approval ask.

I'll copy Maria once we have the mitigation plan.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior AM, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Spike in latency / errors — CobaltPay Reserved pool impact

David / Aditya — forwarding customer details. Attaching a short ops log excerpt from our console (ops_log_excerpt.txt).

Relevant context for triage:
- Account has a Dedicated pool (reserved) with a modest headroom buffer; historically stable for their workload.
- We rolled a runtime performance tweak (attention-kernel swap) to the fleet two days ago; patch was behind a feature flag but might have toggled for certain clusters.
- CobaltPay uses high-batch endpoints for payment orchestration (long prompts, large batch sizes).

Please check these items and report back ASAP:
1) Dedicated pool utilization and per-GPU load for clusters handling CobaltPay (showing per-minute metrics).
2) KV/prefix cache hit rates and memory pressure during the spike window.
3) Any recent quantization or compilation selection that could increase per-token time.
4) Autoscale logs: did their reserved allotment mismatch against actual QPS due to reservation drift or routing policy?

If noisy neighbor is confirmed: propose immediate mitigations (route to hosted L2, enable per-route QPS throttles, or apply burst credits).

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops_log_excerpt.txt

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Spike in latency / errors — CobaltPay Reserved pool impact

Quick findings from initial triage (summary):
- Observed an abrupt increase in token-generation times starting 2026-09-19 02:58 UTC on the cluster serving CobaltPay. The spike correlated with a sustained rise in batch sizes for their primary route; batch sizing jumped ~4x due to a recent client-side SDK change to batch aggressively for throughput.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 88% -> 42% in the same window; memory pressure forced more frequent KV reloads and increased per-token kernel invocations.
- We also observed cross-tenant spillover: one background large-batch internal job simultaneously expanded and consumed shared GPU headroom (noisy neighbor).
- Reserved capacity report: reservation markers were present but the cluster-level autoscaler applied backpressure because effective QPS exceeded the pinned token allocation calculation (reservation drift + a bug in the rate accounting for batched requests).

Immediate mitigations we've applied or can apply now:
A) Throttle per-route batching for CobaltPay via routing policy (limits max-batch-size to 32) — deployable in 10m, expected p95 latency improvement in 15–30m.
B) Apply reserved burst allotment (temporary +10% GPU share) from adjacent low-utilized pools — requires exec sign-off; estimated 2 hours of additional headroom.
C) Fall back to a slightly smaller model variant (L2-quantized) for non-critical routes to free up capacity — can be staged in 20–40m with minimal quality regression.
D) Patch queued: a short fix for the rate-accounting bug (INF-4129) will prevent future reservation drift; ETA for deploy to prod ~48 hours.

Request: Marissa/Tessa, please authorize (B) so we can buy immediate breathing room while we throttle and stage fallback. If we cannot get exec approval quickly, we should proceed with (A) + (C) immediately and present impact/rollback options to the customer.

Logs attached and a short snippet below for context:
"[2026-09-19T03:05:12Z] cluster-a: batch_size=128, kv_hit=0.41, gpu_util=92%"

-David
David Kim
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@cobaltpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in latency / errors — CobaltPay Reserved pool impact

Hi Maria — thanks for the detail and the patience. Internal triage completed and we have a mitigation plan we can enact immediately. High-level summary for your operations team: 

What happened (short):
- A recent client-side change increased batch sizes which, combined with a coincident background job on the same cluster, caused KV cache misses and GPU headroom exhaustion. Our reservation markers were present but our rate-accounting under-counted batched requests (we have a bug logged INF-4129).

Immediate actions we're taking (now -> next 60 minutes):
1) We will apply a per-route max-batch-size cap (32) to your high-throughput endpoints — expected to reduce p95 latency within 15–30m.
2) We're staging a fallback to the L2-quantized model for non-payment-critical routes (will be staged gradually in 20–40m).
3) With Marissa's approval, we'll allocate a temporary +10% reserved burst from low-utilization pools to your Dedicated reservation for a 2-hour window to smooth the immediate backlog.

Compensations & next steps:
- We'll provide a one-off service credit for the impacted window and are ready to extend additional short credits if the business impact estimate from CobaltPay ops warrants it.
- David is tracking a patch for the rate-accounting bug; target production deploy within 48 hours.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute post-mitigation call in 2 hours and a broader technical retrofit review in 3 business days.

Can you confirm you authorize the temporary routing caps and accept a scheduled fallback for non-critical routes? We'll only change critical payment routes with explicit sign-off.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior AM, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-mitigation-plan.pdf

From: Maria Alvarez <maria@cobaltpay.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-lead@cobaltpay.com
Date: 2026-09-20T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in latency / errors — CobaltPay Reserved pool impact

Tessa / Team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Please proceed with A + C immediately (batch cap + L2 fallback for non-critical routes). We approve temporary routing caps for the high-throughput endpoints.

We also accept the temporary burst allocation (B) — Marissa/Redwood, please proceed with the +10% for 2 hours and notify our ops lead when it begins. We'll assess business impact and confirm if further credits are needed.

We'll join the 30-min post-mitigation call in 2 hours. Please include the runbook in the meeting invite.

-Maria
